newsitem.title: USA: MCA in talks to sell Putnam Berkley publisher.
newsitem.headline: MCA in talks to sell Putnam Berkley publisher.

text.p: MCA Inc., the entertainment division of Seagram Co. Ltd., is in talks to sell its Putnam Berkley Publishing Group to Pearson Plc for more than $300 million, people familiar with the talks said Monday.

Pearson, a British-based media and entertainment company that controls the Financial Times newspaper, bought HarperCollins Educational publishing earlier this year from News Corp. for $580 million. Pearson already owns Penguin Group Book Publishers.
The sources said that MCA and Pearson had a number of details to resolve, including the timing of the sale.
An MCA spokeswoman declined to comment on a possible deal. Pearson officials were not immediately available.

Industry analysts said that because Putnam Berkley was a small part of Seagram's total business, it might be sold at the right price. Seagram has not focused on Putnam Berkley since acquiring an 80 percent stake in MCA from Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd. for $5.7 billion last year, they said.

Putnam Berkley Group's authors include Tom Clancy ("Executive Orders"), Patricia Cornwell ("Cause of Death"), Dick Francis ("To the Hilt"), Robin Cook ("Chromosome 6") and Lawrence Sanders ("McNally's Puzzle").

"It's such a small segment of the overall business that it's not an absolutely necessary part of business," said Jeff Logsdon at Cruttenden Roth. "It can be collaborative part, even though historically MCA did not take advantage of it."
Chris Dixon, analyst at PaineWebber Inc., said if cash flow at Putnam was around $30 million, a sale should fetch about $360 million.
Putnam's cash flow is difficult to measure because in financial reports Seagram provides figures only for publishing as a whole, which also includes its Spencer Gifts retail stores.
Cash from a sale "could be deployed in a variety of ways and clearly to the degree they've decided they can better use those funds, they are going to do so," Dixon said.
He noted the company would have to consider several issues, such as taxes, before deciding whether to go ahead.

In the five months ended June 30, Seagram reported sales from entertainment and beverages of $5.0 billion. Publishing, which includes its Spencer Gifts retail operation, generated $264 million in sales, or just over 5 percent of the total.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the company totalled $518 million in the five months ended June 30, and publishing comprised a mere $7.0 million of the total, according to company reports.
MCA is in the movie, television, music, publishing and theme park businesses.
